translations.literal: Qian Liu asked that the Zhenhai army be moved to Hangzhou; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu asked to move the Zhenhai army to Hangzhou; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 復以李茂貞為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen was again made Fengxiang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen was again appointed military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 三月，己丑，以王審知充威武留後。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jichou, Wang Shenzhi was appointed acting military governor of Weiwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jichou, the court appointed Wang Shenzhi acting military governor of Weiwu.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣副使萬年韋震入奏事，求兼鎮天平，朝廷未之許，震力爭之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent his deputy envoy Wei Zhen of Wannian to enter court and report affairs, asking also to hold Tianping; the court did not grant it, and Zhen argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent his deputy envoy Wei Zhen of Wannian to court to report affairs and request concurrent control of Tianping; the court refused, and Wei Zhen pressed the matter hard.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不得已，以全忠為宣武、宣義、天平三鎮節度使。

translations.literal: The court, having no choice, made Quanzhong military governor of the three circuits of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, and Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: The court, having no choice, made Zhu Quanzhong military governor of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, and Tianping.

sentences.zh: 全忠以震為天平留後，以前台州刺史李振為天平節度副使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong made Zhen acting military governor of Tianping and the former Taizhou prefect Li Zhen deputy military governor of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong appointed Wei Zhen acting military governor of Tianping and former Taizhou prefect Li Zhen deputy military governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 振，抱真之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhen was the great-grandson of Baozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen was the great-grandson of Li Baozhen.

sentences.zh: 淮南將周本救蘇州，兩浙將顧全武擊破之。

translations.literal: Huainan general Zhou Ben came to relieve Suzhou; Liang-Zhe general Gu Quanwu defeated and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan general Zhou Ben marched to relieve Suzhou; Liang-Zhe general Gu Quanwu defeated and routed him.

sentences.zh: 淮南將秦裴以兵三千人拔昆山而戍之。

translations.literal: Huainan general Qin Pei with three thousand troops took Kunshan and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan general Qin Pei took Kunshan with three thousand men and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 以潭州刺史、判湖南軍府事馬殷知武安留後。

translations.literal: Tanzhou prefect and acting administrator of Hunan military headquarters Ma Yin was made acting military governor of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou prefect and acting administrator of Hunan military headquarters Ma Yin was appointed acting military governor of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 時湖南管內七州，賊帥楊師遠據衡州，唐世旻據永州，蔡結據道州，陳彥謙據郴州，魯景仁據連州，殷所得惟潭、邵而已。

translations.literal: At the time Hunan administered seven prefectures within its borders; bandit chiefs Yang Shiyuan held Hengzhou, Tang Shimin held Yongzhou, Cai Jie held Daozhou, Chen Yanqian held Chenzhou, and Lu Jingren held Lianzhou—of these, Yin held only Tan and Shao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hunan nominally comprised seven prefectures, but bandit chiefs Yang Shiyuan held Hengzhou, Tang Shimin held Yongzhou, Cai Jie held Daozhou, Chen Yanqian held Chenzhou, and Lu Jingren held Lianzhou; Ma Yin controlled only Tan and Shao.

sentences.zh: 義昌節度使盧彥威，性殘虐，又不禮於鄰道。

translations.literal: Yichang military governor Lu Yanwei was by nature cruel and tyrannical and also showed no courtesy to neighboring circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yichang military governor Lu Yanwei was cruel and overbearing and showed no courtesy to neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 與盧龍節度使劉仁恭爭鹽利，仁恭遣其子守文將兵襲滄州，彥威棄城，挈家奔魏州。

translations.literal: He contended with Lulong military governor Liu Rengong over salt profits; Rengong sent his son Shouwen to lead troops in a surprise attack on Cangzhou; Yanwei abandoned the city and fled with his family to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with Lulong military governor Liu Rengong over salt revenues; Liu Rengong sent his son Shouwen to raid Cangzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled with his family to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 羅弘信不納，乃奔汴州。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxin would not receive him, so he fled to Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin would not take him in, so he fled to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁恭遂取滄、景、德三州，以守文為義昌留後。

translations.literal: Rengong thereupon took the three prefectures of Cang, Jing, and De and made Shouwen acting military governor of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong then seized Cang, Jing, and De and appointed Shouwen acting military governor of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 仁恭兵勢益盛，自謂得天助，有併吞河朔之志，為守文請旌節，朝廷未許。

translations.literal: Rengong's military power grew ever greater; he claimed Heaven's aid and harbored the ambition to swallow the Hebei region; he memorialized that Shouwen be granted the commander's banner and staff, but the court did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong's armies grew stronger; he claimed Heaven's favor and aimed to swallow the Hebei region; he asked the court to grant Shouwen a commission, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 會中使至范陽，仁恭語之曰：「旌節吾自有之，但欲得長安本色耳，何為累章見拒，為吾言之！」

translations.literal: When a palace envoy reached Fanyang, Rengong said to him: "The banner and staff I already have of my own; I only want the genuine Chang'an article—why refuse me with repeated memorials? Speak for me!"
translations.idiomatic: When a palace envoy reached Fanyang, Liu Rengong told him, "I already have my own command; I only want the genuine commission from Chang'an—why refuse me memorial after memorial? Put in a word for me!"

sentences.zh: 其悖慢如此。

translations.literal: His insolence went so far.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠與劉仁恭修好，會魏博兵擊李克用。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong made peace with Liu Rengong, and together with Weibo troops attacked Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong reconciled with Liu Rengong and, together with Weibo forces, attacked Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁未，全忠至巨鹿城下，敗河東兵萬餘人，遂北至青山口。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingwei, Quanzhong reached below the walls of Julu, defeated more than ten thousand Hedong troops, and then marched north to Qingshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingwei, Zhu Quanzhong reached Julu, defeated more than ten thousand Hedong troops, and marched north to Qingshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 以護國節度使王珂兼侍中。

translations.literal: Huguo military governor Wang Ke was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave Huguo military governor Wang Ke the additional title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，朱全忠遣葛從周分兵攻洺州，戊辰，拔之，斬刺史邢善益。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Zhu Quanzhong sent Ge Congzhou with divided forces to attack Mozhou; on wuchen it was taken, and prefect Xing Shanyi was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Zhu Quanzhong sent Ge Congzhou with detached columns against Mozhou; on wuchen it fell, and prefect Xing Shanyi was executed.

sentences.zh: 五月，己巳朔，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the jisi new moon, the realm was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the jisi new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 葛從周攻邢州，刺史馬師素棄城走。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou attacked Xingzhou; prefect Ma Shisu abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou attacked Xingzhou; Ma Shisu abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 辛未，磁州刺史袁奉滔自剄。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Cizhou prefect Yuan Fengtao slit his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Cizhou prefect Yuan Fengtao committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 全忠以從周為昭義留後，守邢、洺、磁三州而還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong made Congzhou acting military governor of Zhaoyi, left him to hold the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong appointed Ge Congzhou acting military governor of Zhaoyi, left him holding Xing, Ming, and Ci, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以武定節度使李繼密為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Wuding military governor Li Jimi was made Shannan West Circuit military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wuding military governor Li Jimi was appointed military governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞王建已用王宗滌為東川留後，乃召劉崇望還，為兵部尚書，仍以宗滌為留後。

translations.literal: The court heard that Wang Jian had already appointed Wang Zongdi acting military governor of Dongchuan, so it summoned Liu Chongwang back and made him Minister of War, yet still left Zongdi as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wang Jian had already installed Wang Zongdi as acting military governor of Dongchuan, the court recalled Liu Chongwang and made him Minister of War, but still recognized Zongdi as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 湖南將姚彥章言於馬殷，請取衡、永、道、連、郴五州，仍薦李瓊為將。

translations.literal: Hunan general Yao Yanzhang spoke to Ma Yin, asking to take the five prefectures of Heng, Yong, Dao, Lian, and Chen, and also recommending Li Qiong as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan general Yao Yanzhang urged Ma Yin to seize Heng, Yong, Dao, Lian, and Chen, and recommended Li Qiong to lead the campaign.

sentences.zh: 殷以瓊及秦彥暉為嶺北七州游奕使，張圖英、李唐副之，將兵攻衡州，斬楊師遠，引兵趣永州，圍之月餘，唐世旻走死。

translations.literal: Yin made Qiong and Qin Yanhui roaming inspectors of the seven northern Ling prefectures, with Zhang Tuying and Li Tang as deputies; they led troops to attack Hengzhou, beheaded Yang Shiyuan, then marched on Yongzhou, besieged it for more than a month, and Tang Shimin fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin made Li Qiong and Qin Yanhui roaming inspectors of the seven northern Ling prefectures, with Zhang Tuying and Li Tang as deputies; they attacked Hengzhou, killed Yang Shiyuan, then marched on Yongzhou, besieged it for more than a month, and Tang Shimin fled to his death.

sentences.zh: 殷以李唐為永州刺史。

translations.literal: Yin made Li Tang prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin appointed Li Tang prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，以濠州刺史趙珝為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Haozhou prefect Zhao Xu was made Zhongwu military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Haozhou prefect Zhao Xu was appointed military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 珝，犨之弟也。

translations.literal: Xu was the younger brother of Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xu was the younger brother of Zhao Chao.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，加武貞節度使雷滿同平章事，加鎮南節度使鍾傳兼侍中。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wuzhen military governor Lei Man was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councillor, and Zhennan military governor Zhong Chuan was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the court promoted Wuzhen military governor Lei Man to Co-Grand Councillor and Zhennan military governor Zhong Chuan to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 忠義節度使趙匡凝聞朱全忠有清口之敗，陰附於楊行密。

translations.literal: Zhongyi military governor Zhao Kuangning heard that Zhu Quanzhong had suffered defeat at Qingkou and secretly attached himself to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi military governor Zhao Kuangning heard of Zhu Quanzhong's defeat at Qingkou and secretly aligned himself with Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣宿州刺史尉氏氏叔琮將兵伐之，丙申，拔唐州，擒隨州刺史趙匡璘，敗襄州兵於鄧城。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Suzhou prefect Shi Shuzong of Weishi to lead troops against him; on bingshen he took Tangzhou, captured Suizhou prefect Zhao Kuanglin, and defeated Xiangzhou troops at Dengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Suzhou prefect Shi Shuzong of Weishi against him; on bingshen he took Tangzhou, captured Suizhou prefect Zhao Kuanglin, and routed Xiangzhou troops at Dengcheng.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，改華州為興德府。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengxu, Huazhou was changed to Xingde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengxu, Huazhou was redesignated Xingde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊午，汴將康懷貞襲鄧州，克之，擒刺史國湘。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Bian general Kang Huaizhen made a surprise attack on Dengzhou, took it, and captured prefect Guo Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Bian general Kang Huaizhen stormed Dengzhou, took it, and captured prefect Guo Xiang.

sentences.zh: 趙匡凝懼，遣使請服於朱全忠，全忠許之。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangning was afraid, sent an envoy to ask to submit to Zhu Quanzhong, and Quanzhong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning was afraid, sent envoys to submit to Zhu Quanzhong, and Zhu Quanzhong accepted.

sentences.zh: 己未，車駕發華州。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the imperial carriage set out from Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the emperor left Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，至長安。

translations.literal: On renxu, it reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, he reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 甲子，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the realm was pardoned and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 上欲籓鎮相與輯睦，以太子賓客張有孚為河東、汴州宣慰使，賜李克用、朱全忠詔，又令宰相與之書，使之和解。

translations.literal: The emperor wished the frontier governors to live in harmony with one another; he made Crown Prince's Guest Zhang Youfu pacification envoy to Hedong and Bianzhou, bestowed edicts on Li Keyong and Zhu Quanzhong, and also ordered the chief ministers to write them letters urging reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted the regional governors to live at peace; he appointed Crown Prince's Guest Zhang Youfu pacification envoy to Hedong and Bianzhou, sent edicts to Li Keyong and Zhu Quanzhong, and had the chief ministers write them as well, urging reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 克用欲奉詔，而恥於先自屈，乃致書王鎔，使通於全忠。

translations.literal: Keyong wished to obey the edict but was ashamed to yield first; he therefore wrote Wang Rong, asking him to open communication with Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong wished to obey the edict but was ashamed to yield first; he wrote Wang Rong, asking him to open talks with Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠不從。

translations.literal: Quanzhong would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong refused.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙亥，加韓建守太傅、興德尹，加王鎔兼中書令，羅弘信守侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yihai, Han Jian was given the additional posts of Grand Mentor and Mayor of Xingde; Wang Rong was given the additional title of Director of the Secretariat; Luo Hongxin was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yihai, Han Jian was made Grand Mentor and Mayor of Xingde; Wang Rong was given the additional title of Director of the Secretariat; Luo Hongxin was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 己丑，東川留後王宗滌言於王建，以東川封疆五千里，文移往還，動逾數月，請分遂、合、瀘、渝、昌五州別為一鎮，建表言之。

translations.literal: On jichou, Dongchuan acting military governor Wang Zongdi spoke to Wang Jian: the Dongchuan domain was five thousand li, and documents going back and forth often took months; he asked that the five prefectures of Sui, He, Lu, Yu, and Chang be separated into another command; Jian memorialized this.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, acting Dongchuan military governor Wang Zongdi told Wang Jian that the circuit spanned five thousand li and official correspondence took months in transit; he asked that Sui, He, Lu, Yu, and Chang be split off as a separate command, and Wang Jian memorialized the request.

sentences.zh: 顧全武攻蘇州，城中及援兵食皆盡。

translations.literal: Gu Quanwu attacked Suzhou; within the city and among the relief troops, food was all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Quanwu besieged Suzhou until the city and its relief forces had eaten through their stores.

sentences.zh: 甲申，淮南所署蘇州刺史台濛棄城走，援兵亦遁。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Tai Meng, whom Huainan had appointed prefect of Suzhou, abandoned the city and fled, and the relief troops also scattered.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Tai Meng, whom Huainan had appointed prefect of Suzhou, abandoned the city and fled, and the relief army melted away.

sentences.zh: 全武克蘇州，追敗周本等於望亭。

translations.literal: Quanwu took Suzhou and pursued, defeating Zhou Ben and others at Wangting.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Quanwu took Suzhou and routed Zhou Ben and the others at Wangting.

sentences.zh: 獨秦裴守昆山不下，全武帥萬餘人攻之。

translations.literal: Only Qin Pei held Kunshan and would not yield; Quanwu led more than ten thousand men to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Qin Pei still held Kunshan; Gu Quanwu led more than ten thousand men against it.

sentences.zh: 裴屢出戰，使病者被甲執矛，壯者彀弓弩，全武每為之卻。

translations.literal: Pei repeatedly came out to fight, having the sick don armor and grasp spears while the strong drew bows and crossbows; each time Quanwu was driven back.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Pei sallied again and again, putting the sick in armor with spears and the able-bodied behind bows and crossbows; each time Gu Quanwu was forced back.

sentences.zh: 全武檄裴令降。

translations.literal: Quanwu sent a proclamation ordering Pei to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Quanwu sent a summons demanding Qin Pei's surrender.

sentences.zh: 全武嘗為僧，裴封函納款，全武喜，召諸將發函，乃佛經一卷，全武大慚，曰：「裴不憂死，何暇戲予！」

translations.literal: Quanwu had once been a monk; Pei sealed a letter of submission in a case and presented it; Quanwu was pleased and summoned his generals to open the case—it was but one scroll of Buddhist scripture; Quanwu was deeply ashamed and said: "Pei does not fear death—how has he leisure to mock me!"
translations.idiomatic: Gu Quanwu had once been a monk; Qin Pei sent a sealed case with a letter of surrender; delighted, Gu Quanwu gathered his generals to open it—it held a single scroll of Buddhist scripture; deeply ashamed, he said, "Qin Pei does not fear death—how does he find time to mock me!"

sentences.zh: 益兵攻城，引水灌之，城壞，食盡，裴乃降。

translations.literal: He added troops to assault the city, diverted water to flood it, the walls collapsed, food was exhausted, and Pei then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He brought up more troops, diverted water to flood the city, breached the walls, and when supplies ran out Qin Pei surrendered.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐設千人饌以待之，及出，羸兵不滿百人。

translations.literal: Qian Liu set out a feast for a thousand men to await him; when Pei came out, his emaciated troops numbered fewer than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu prepared a feast for a thousand men to receive him; when Qin Pei marched out, his wasted garrison numbered fewer than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 鏐怒曰：「單弱如此，何敢久為旅拒！」

translations.literal: Liu said angrily: "So feeble as this—how did you dare hold out as a guest in resistance so long!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu said angrily, "So few and weak as this—how did you dare hold out against us so long!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「裴義不負楊公，今力屈而降耳，非心降也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Pei in righteousness did not fail Lord Yang; now, strength spent, I yield—that is all; it is not surrender of the heart."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In duty I did not fail Lord Yang; now, strength spent, I yield—that is all. This is not surrender of the heart."

sentences.zh: 鏐善其言。

translations.literal: Liu approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu admired his answer.

sentences.zh: 顧全武亦勸鏐宥之，鏐從之。

translations.literal: Gu Quanwu also urged Liu to spare him, and Liu complied.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Quanwu also urged Qian Liu to spare him, and Qian Liu agreed.

sentences.zh: 時人稱全武長者。

translations.literal: People of the time praised Quanwu as a man of mature character.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised Gu Quanwu as a man of magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使羅弘信薨，軍中推其子節度副使紹威知留後。

translations.literal: Weibo military governor Luo Hongxin died; the army pushed his son, deputy military governor Shaowei, to serve as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo military governor Luo Hongxin died; the army installed his son, deputy military governor Luo Shaowei, as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 汴將朱友恭將兵還自江、淮，過安州，或告刺史武瑜潛與淮南通，謀取汴軍，冬，十月，己亥，友恭攻而殺之。

translations.literal: Bian general Zhu Yougong was leading troops back from the Jiang-Huai region and passed through Anzhou; someone reported that prefect Wu Yu was secretly in communication with Huainan and plotted to seize the Bian troops; in winter, the tenth month, on jihai, Yougong attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bian general Zhu Yougong was marching back from the Jiang-Huai region through Anzhou when someone reported that prefect Wu Yu was secretly dealing with Huainan and plotting to seize the Bian army; in winter, the tenth month, on jihai, Zhu Yougong attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣其將李嗣昭、周德威將步騎二萬出青山，將復山東三州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent his generals Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry out from Qingshan, intending to recover the three Shandong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent his generals Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei with twenty thousand foot and horse out of Qingshan Pass, intending to recover the three eastern prefectures.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，進攻邢州，葛從周出戰，大破之。

translations.literal: On renyin, they pressed the attack on Xingzhou; Ge Congzhou went out to fight and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the army pressed the attack on Xingzhou; Ge Congzhou gave battle and routed them.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭等引兵退入青山，從周追之，將扼其歸路。

translations.literal: Sizhao and the others led the army in retreat into Qingshan; Congzhou pursued them, about to choke off their route of return.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao and the others withdrew into the Green Mountains; Ge Congzhou pursued, intending to cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 步兵自潰，嗣昭不能制。

translations.literal: The foot soldiers collapsed on their own; Sizhao could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry broke on their own; Li Sizhao could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 會橫衝都將李嗣源以所部兵至，謂嗣昭曰：「吾輩亦去，則勢不可支矣，我試為公擊之。」

translations.literal: At this moment Li Siyuan, commander of the Vanguard Assault Corps, arrived with the troops under his command and said to Sizhao, "If we leave too, the situation cannot be sustained; let me try to strike them for you."
translations.idiomatic: Just then Li Siyuan, commander of the Vanguard Assault Corps, arrived with his troops and said to Li Sizhao, "If we withdraw as well, our position will collapse; let me try to hit them for you."

sentences.zh: 嗣昭曰：「善，我請從公後。」

translations.literal: Sizhao said, "Good; I ask to follow behind you."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao said, "Very well; I will follow behind you."

sentences.zh: 嗣源乃解鞍厲鏃，乘高佈陣，左右指畫，邢隊莫之測。

translations.literal: Siyuan then loosed saddles and sharpened arrowheads, took the high ground and deployed formations, pointing and arranging left and right; the Xingzhou ranks could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan then had saddles removed and arrowheads honed, took the high ground and deployed his formation, directing movements to left and right; Ge Congzhou's troops could not guess his intent.

sentences.zh: 嗣源直前奮擊，嗣昭繼之，從周乃退。

translations.literal: Siyuan charged straight ahead and struck fiercely; Sizhao followed him; Congzhou then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan charged ahead at full force; Li Sizhao came up behind him; Ge Congzhou then pulled back.

sentences.zh: 德威，馬邑人也。

translations.literal: Dewei was a man of Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei was a native of Mayi.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以威武留後王審知為節度使。

translations.literal: On guimao, Military Commissioner Wang Shenzhi of Weiwu was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Wang Shenzhi, acting military governor of Weiwu, was appointed full military governor.

sentences.zh: 以羅紹威知魏博留後。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei was made acting military governor of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei was made acting military governor of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以東川留後王宗滌為節度使。

translations.literal: On disi, Acting Military Governor Wang Zongdi of Dongchuan was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On disi, Wang Zongdi, acting military governor of Dongchuan, was appointed full military governor.

sentences.zh: 加佑國節度使張全義兼侍中。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyi, military governor of Youguo, was additionally made attendant grand master.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi, military governor of Youguo, was also appointed attendant grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 王珙引汴兵寇河中，王珂告急於李克用。

translations.literal: Wang Gong led Bian troops to raid Hezhong; Wang Ke reported the emergency to Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong led Bian troops against Hezhong; Wang Ke urgently appealed to Li Keyong for aid.

sentences.zh: 克用遣李嗣昭救之，敗汴兵於胡壁，汴人走。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Li Sizhao to rescue him; he defeated Bian troops at Hubi; the Bian men fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent Li Sizhao to the rescue; Li Sizhao routed the Liang army at Hubi, and the Liang forces fled.

sentences.zh: 前常州刺史王柷，性剛介，有時望。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, former prefect of Changzhou, was by nature stern and upright, and enjoyed esteem in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, former prefect of Changzhou, was stern and upright and enjoyed wide repute.

sentences.zh: 詔征之，時人以為且入相。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him; men of the age thought he would soon enter the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him by edict; contemporaries expected he would soon join the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 過陝，王珙延奉甚至，請敘子侄之禮拜之，柷固辭不受。

translations.literal: Passing through Shan prefecture, Wang Gong entertained him with utmost ceremony and asked to pay him respects in the formality of nephew to uncle; Zhi firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed through Shanzhou, Wang Gong entertained him with extreme courtesy and asked to receive him with ceremony befitting a nephew before an uncle; Wang Zhi steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 珙怒，使送者殺之，並其家人悉投諸河，掠其資裝，以覆舟聞。

translations.literal: Gong grew angry, had the escort kill him, threw his entire family into the river, plundered his belongings, and reported it as a capsized boat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong, enraged, had his escort murder him, drowned his entire family in the Yellow River, seized his possessions, and reported that his boat had overturned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不敢詰。

translations.literal: The court did not dare to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not dare investigate.

sentences.zh: 閏月，錢鏐以其將曹圭為蘇州制置使，遣王球攻婺州。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Qian Liu made his general Cao Gui commissioner for Suzhou and dispatched Wang Qiu to attack Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Qian Liu made his general Cao Gui commissioner for organizing Suzhou and sent Wang Qiu to attack Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲寅，立皇子禎為雅王，祥為瓊王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiayin, the princes Zhen and Xiang were established as Prince of Ya and Prince of Qiong respectively.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiayin, Imperial Prince Zhen was named Prince of Ya and Imperial Prince Xiang was named Prince of Qiong.

sentences.zh: 以魏博留後羅紹威為節度使。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei, acting military governor of Weibo, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei was promoted from acting military governor to full military governor of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 衢州刺史陳岌請降於楊行密，錢鏐使顧全武討之。

translations.literal: Chen Ji, prefect of Quzhou, asked to surrender to Yang Xingmi; Qian Liu sent Gu Quanwu to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou prefect Chen Ji offered to surrender to Yang Xingmi; Qian Liu sent Gu Quanwu to attack him.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠以奉國節度使崔洪與楊行密交通，遣其將張存敬攻之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong, because Fengguo military governor Cui Hong was in contact with Yang Xingmi, sent his general Zhang Cunjing to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fengguo military governor Cui Hong was in league with Yang Xingmi, Zhu Quanzhong sent his general Zhang Cunjing to attack him.

sentences.zh: 洪懼，請以弟都指揮使賢為質，且言：「將士頑悍，不受節制，請遣二千人詣麾下從征伐。」

translations.literal: Hong was afraid, asked to send his younger brother Xian, commander-in-chief of the capital guard, as hostage, and added, "The officers and soldiers are obstinate and fierce and do not obey control; please send two thousand men to your headquarters to follow in campaigns."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong was terrified; he offered his younger brother Xian, chief commander of the guard, as a hostage, and said, "My troops are unruly and will not obey orders; please take two thousand of them into your service for campaigns abroad."

sentences.zh: 全忠許之，召存敬還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong agreed, and summoned Cunjing back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong agreed and recalled Zhang Cunjing.

sentences.zh: 存敬，曹州人也。

translations.literal: Cunjing was a man of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunjing was a native of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，昭義節度使薛志勤薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Zhaoyi military governor Xue Zhiqin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Zhaoyi military governor Xue Zhiqin died.

sentences.zh: 李克用之平王行瑜也，李罕之求邠寧於克用。

translations.literal: When Li Keyong pacified Wang Xingyu, Li Hanzhi asked Keyong for Binning.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Keyong had suppressed Wang Xingyu, Li Hanzhi asked him for the Binning circuit.

sentences.zh: 克用曰：「行瑜恃功邀君，故吾與公討而誅之。

translations.literal: Keyong said, "Xingyu relied on his achievements to press you; therefore I joined with you to campaign against him and put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong said, "Xingyu used his merits to bully you; that is why I joined you in campaigning against him and executing him.

sentences.zh: 昨破賊之日，吾首奏趣蘇文建赴鎮。

translations.literal: On the day we defeated the rebels yesterday, I first memorialized urging Su Wenjian to proceed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When we defeated the rebels, I was the first to memorialize urging Su Wenjian to take up his post at the circuit.

sentences.zh: 今才達天聽，遽復二三，朝野之論，必喧然謂吾輩復如行瑜所為也。

translations.literal: Now it has only just reached the imperial ear, yet abruptly there are again two or three such cases; court and countryside opinion will surely clamor that we are again doing as Xingyu did.
translations.idiomatic: That word has only just reached the throne; if we suddenly raise two or three more such cases, court and public opinion will surely clamor that we are doing again what Xingyu did.

sentences.zh: 吾與公情如同體，固無所愛，俟還鎮，當更為公論功賞所為也。

translations.literal: My feeling toward you, sir, is as one body; I truly begrudge nothing; when I return to my post, I shall again discuss your merits and reward what you have done.
translations.idiomatic: You and I are of one heart; I withhold nothing from you; once I return to my territory, I will again weigh your achievements and reward what you have accomplished.

sentences.zh: 吾與公情如同體，固無所愛，俟還鎮，當更為公論功賞耳。」

translations.literal: My feeling toward you, sir, is as one body; I truly begrudge nothing; when I return to my post, I shall again discuss your merits and grant reward, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: You and I are of one heart; I withhold nothing from you; once I return to my territory, I will again weigh your merits and see you rewarded—that is all."

sentences.zh: 罕之不悅而退，私於蓋寓曰：「罕之自河陽失守，依托大庇，歲月已深。

translations.literal: Hanzhi withdrew displeased, and privately said to Gai Yu, "Since Hanzhi lost Heyang, I have relied on great shelter; the months and years have run deep.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi withdrew in displeasure and privately told Gai Yu, "Since I lost Heyang I have relied on His Highness's protection; many years have passed.

sentences.zh: 比來衰老，倦於軍旅，若蒙吾王與太傅哀愍，賜一小鎮，使數年之間休兵養疾，然後歸老閭閻，倖免。」

translations.literal: Lately I have grown old and weary of military affairs; if Our King and the Grand Tutor would show pity and grace, grant me a small prefecture, let me cease arms and nurse illness for some years, then return in old age to my village lanes—the good fortune of escape."
translations.idiomatic: I am aging now and tired of campaigning; if my lord the Prince and the Grand Tutor would show mercy and grant me a small command, let me lay down arms and nurse my illness for a few years, then go home to die in peace."

sentences.zh: 寓為之言，克用不應。

translations.literal: Yu spoke on his behalf; Keyong did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Yu pleaded his case; Li Keyong did not answer.

sentences.zh: 每籓鎮缺，議不及罕之，罕之甚鬱鬱。

translations.literal: Whenever a circuit post fell vacant, discussion never reached Hanzhi; Hanzhi was very depressed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a military governorship fell vacant, Li Hanzhi's name was never raised; he grew deeply despondent.

sentences.zh: 寓恐其有它志，亟為之言，克用曰：「吾於罕之豈愛一鎮，但罕之，鷹也，饑則為用，飽則背飛。」

translations.literal: Yu feared he had another intent and urgently spoke for him; Keyong said, "How could I begrudge Hanzhi one prefecture? But Hanzhi is a hawk: hungry, he serves; full, he flies against you."
translations.idiomatic: Gai Yu feared other designs and pressed his case again; Li Keyong said, "It is not that I begrudge Li Hanzhi a circuit—but Li Hanzhi is a hawk: useful when hungry, and when fed he flies away."

sentences.zh: 及志勤薨，旬日無帥，罕之擅引澤州兵夜入潞州，據之，以狀白克用，曰：「薛鐵山死，州民無主，慮不逞者為變，故罕之專命鎮撫，取王裁旨。」

translations.literal: When Zhiqin died, for ten days there was no commander; Hanzhi on his own authority led Zezhou troops by night into Luzhou and seized it; he reported the situation to Keyong, saying, "Iron Mountain Xue is dead; the people of the prefecture have no master; I feared the unruly would make trouble, so Hanzhi took sole command to pacify them, begging the Prince's ruling."
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Zhiqin died the circuit went ten days without a commander; Li Hanzhi on his own led Zezhou troops into Luzhou by night and seized it. He reported to Li Keyong, saying, "Iron Mountain Xue is dead; Luzhou has no chief; I feared trouble from malcontents, so I took command myself to pacify the region and beg your decision, my lord."

sentences.zh: 克用怒，遣人讓之。

translations.literal: Keyong was angry and sent someone to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was furious and sent a messenger to reproach him.

sentences.zh: 罕之遂遣其子顥請降於朱全忠，執河東將馬溉等及沁州刺史傅瑤送汴州。

translations.literal: Hanzhi thereupon sent his son Hao to ask to surrender to Zhu Quanzhong, seized the Hedong generals Ma Gai and others and Qinzhou prefect Fu Yao, and sent them to Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi then sent his son Hao to offer surrender to Zhu Quanzhong, seized Hedong generals including Ma Gai and Qinzhou prefect Fu Yao, and sent them as captives to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 克用遣李嗣昭將兵討之，嗣昭先取澤州，收罕之家屬送晉陽。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Li Sizhao to lead troops against him; Sizhao first took Zezhou and sent Hanzhi's family members to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent Li Sizhao against him; Li Sizhao first seized Zezhou and sent Li Hanzhi's family to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣成及等歸兩浙以易魏約等，錢鏐許之。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent Cheng Ji and others back to the two Zhes in exchange for Wei Yue and others; Qian Liu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi returned Cheng Ji and others to the two Zhes in exchange for Wei Yue and others; Qian Liu agreed.

sentences.zh: 韶州刺史曾兗舉兵攻廣州，州將王鐐帥戰艦應之。

translations.literal: Zeng Yan, prefect of Shaozhou, raised troops to attack Guangzhou; the prefectural general Wang Liao led war-ships to answer him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhou prefect Zeng Yan raised troops and attacked Guangzhou; prefectural officer Wang Liao led warships to join him.

sentences.zh: 清海行軍司馬劉隱一戰破之。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, campaigning marshal of Qinghai, defeated them in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, campaigning deputy of Qinghai, broke them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 韶州將劉潼復據湞、涵，隱討斬之。

translations.literal: The Shaozhou general Liu Tong again occupied Zhen and Han; Yin campaigned and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhou officer Liu Tong seized Zhen and Han again; Liu Yin campaigned against him and executed him.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝中之上光化二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely Solemn Illustrious Cultivated Filial, middle upper, Guanghua second year (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong—the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultivated, and Filial—middle upper, second year of Guanghua (

sentences.zh: 己未，公元八九九年）

translations.literal: jiwei, 899 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiwei, AD 899)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁未，中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事崔胤罷守本官。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingwei, Palace Attendant Cui Yin, concurrently vice director of the ministry of personnel and co–chief minister of the council of state, was relieved and kept his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingwei, Cui Yin was removed as co–chief minister and palace attendant; he retained his post as vice director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書陸扆同平章事。

translations.literal: Lu Yi, director of the ministry of war, was made co–chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi, director of the ministry of war, was appointed co–chief minister.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠表李罕之為昭義節度使，又表權知河陽留後丁會、武寧留後王敬蕘、彰義留後張珂並為節度使。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong memorialized Li Hanzhi as Zhaoyi military governor, and also memorialized Ding Hui, acting governor of Heyang, Wang Jingrao of Wuning, and Zhang Ke of Zhangyi all as military governors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong memorialized that Li Hanzhi be made military governor of Zhaoyi, and that Ding Hui, acting governor of Heyang, Wang Jingrao of Wuning, and Zhang Ke of Zhangyi each be made full military governors.

sentences.zh: 楊行密與朱瑾將兵數萬攻徐州，軍於呂梁，朱全忠遣騎將張歸厚救之。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi and Zhu Jin led tens of thousands of troops to attack Xuzhou and encamped at Lüliang; Zhu Quanzhong sent the cavalry general Zhang Guihou to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi and Zhu Jin led tens of thousands of men against Xuzhou and encamped at Lüliang; Zhu Quanzhong sent cavalry commander Zhang Guihou to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭發幽、滄等十二州兵十萬，欲兼河朔。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong mobilized from You, Cang, and other twelve prefectures one hundred thousand troops, intending to take both sides of the Yellow River northward plain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong raised a hundred thousand men from twelve prefectures including Youzhou and Cangzhou, intending to swallow the Hebei plain.

sentences.zh: 攻貝州，拔之，城中萬餘戶，盡屠之，投屍清水。

translations.literal: He attacked Beizhou, took it; more than ten thousand households in the city were all slaughtered; corpses were thrown into the Clear River.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Beizhou and captured it, then massacred the city's ten thousand-odd households and cast the bodies into the Clear River.

sentences.zh: 由是諸城各堅守不下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various cities each held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every city held firm and could not be reduced.

sentences.zh: 仁恭進攻魏州，營於城北。

translations.literal: Rengong advanced to attack Weizhou and encamped north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong pressed the attack on Weizhou and pitched camp north of the walls.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使羅紹威求救於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Weibo military governor Luo Shaowei begged Zhu Quanzhong for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo military governor Luo Shaowei urgently appealed to Zhu Quanzhong for help.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣崔賢還蔡州，發其兵二千詣大梁。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent Cui Xian back to Caizhou and mobilized two thousand of his troops to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Cui Xian back to Caizhou and dispatched two thousand of his troops to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 二月，蔡將崔景思等殺賢，劫崔洪，悉驅兵民度淮奔楊行密。

translations.literal: In the second month, Cai generals Cui Jingsi and others killed Xian, seized Cui Hong, and drove all soldiers and civilians across the Huai to flee to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Cai generals led by Cui Jingsi murdered Cui Xian, seized Cui Hong, and drove soldiers and civilians across the Huai to join Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 兵民稍稍遁歸，至廣陵者不滿二千人。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians gradually slipped back; those who reached Guangling were fewer than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Troops and civilians gradually straggled back, but fewer than two thousand reached Guangling.

sentences.zh: 全忠命許州刺史朱友裕守蔡州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered Xuzhou prefect Zhu Youyu to hold Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong appointed Zhu Youyu, prefect of Xuzhou, to hold Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠自將救徐州，楊行密聞之，引兵去。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong personally led troops to rescue Xuzhou; Yang Xingmi heard this and withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong marched in person to relieve Xuzhou; when Yang Xingmi learned of it he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 汴人追及之於下邳，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: Bian men overtook them at Xiapi and killed more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liang troops overtook them at Xiapi and killed more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 全忠行至輝州，聞淮南兵已退，乃還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong reached Huizhou, heard that Huainan troops had already withdrawn, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong reached Huizhou, learned that the Huainan army had already withdrawn, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 三月，朱全忠遣其將李思安、張存敬將兵救魏博，屯於內黃。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhu Quanzhong sent his generals Li Si'an and Zhang Cunjing to lead troops to rescue Weibo; they encamped at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhu Quanzhong sent Li Si'an and Zhang Cunjing to relieve Weibo; they encamped at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，全忠以中軍軍於滑州。

translations.literal: On guimao, Quanzhong led the central army to camp at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Zhu Quanzhong established his main force at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭謂其子守文曰：「汝勇十倍于思安，當先虜鼠輩，後擒紹威耳！」

translations.literal: Liu Rengong said to his son Shouwen, "Your courage is ten times that of Si'an; you ought first to capture these rat fellows, then seize Shaowei!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong told his son Shouwen, "You are ten times braver than Li Si'an—you should bag those rats first, then take Shaowei!"

sentences.zh: 乃遣守文及其妹婿單可及將精兵五萬擊思安於內黃。

translations.literal: He then sent Shouwen and his son-in-law Shan Keji to lead fifty thousand picked troops to strike Si'an at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Liu Shouwen and his son-in-law Shan Keji with fifty thousand elite troops to attack Li Si'an at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 丁未，思安使其將袁象先伏兵於清水之右，思安逆戰於繁陽，陽不勝而卻，守文逐之。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Si'an had his general Yuan Xiangxian hide troops on the right bank of the Clear River; Si'an met the enemy in battle at Fanyang, feigned not winning and withdrew; Shouwen pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Li Si'an had Yuan Xiangxian lay ambush on the right bank of the Clear River; Li Si'an gave battle at Fanyang, pretended defeat, and fell back; Liu Shouwen pursued.

sentences.zh: 及內黃之北，思安勒兵還戰，伏兵發，夾擊之。

translations.literal: When north of Neihuang, Si'an reined in the army and turned to fight; the hidden troops sprang up and struck them from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: North of Neihuang, Li Si'an wheeled about and counterattacked; the ambush rose and hit them from both flanks.

sentences.zh: 幽州兵大敗，斬可及，殺獲三萬人，守文僅以身免。

translations.literal: Youzhou troops were greatly defeated; Keji was beheaded; more than thirty thousand were killed or captured; Shouwen barely escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army was routed; Shan Keji was beheaded; thirty thousand were killed or captured; Liu Shouwen barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 可及，幽州驍將，號「單無敵」，燕軍失之喪氣。

translations.literal: Keji was a fierce Youzhou general, called "Shan the Matchless"; the Yan army lost him and their spirits sank.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Keji was a fierce Yan general nicknamed "Shan the Invincible"; his loss drained the army's morale.

sentences.zh: 思安，陳留人也。

translations.literal: Si'an was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'an was a native of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 時葛從周自邢州將精騎八百已入魏州。

translations.literal: At this time Ge Congzhou from Xingzhou with eight hundred picked horsemen had already entered Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By then Ge Congzhou had already entered Weizhou from Xingzhou with eight hundred elite cavalry.

sentences.zh: 戊申，仁恭攻上水關、館陶門。

translations.literal: On wushen, Rengong attacked the Upper Water Gate and the Guantao Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Liu Rengong attacked the Upper Water Gate and the Guantao Gate.

sentences.zh: 從周與宣義牙將賀德倫出戰，顧門者曰：「前有大敵，不可返顧。」

translations.literal: Congzhou and Xuanyi junior general He Delun went out to fight; he looked at the gate guards and said, "Ahead there is a great enemy; you must not look back."
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou and He Delun, a junior general of Xuanyi, rode out to fight; Ge Congzhou told the gate guards, "A great enemy lies ahead—do not look back."

sentences.zh: 命闔其扉。

translations.literal: He ordered the doors shut.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the gates barred shut.

sentences.zh: 從周等殊死戰，仁恭復大敗，擒其將薛突厥、王鄶郎。

translations.literal: Congzhou and the others fought a death struggle; Rengong was again greatly defeated; his generals Xue Tujue and Wang Julang were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou and his men fought to the death; Liu Rengong was routed again; his generals Xue Tujue and Wang Julang were taken.

sentences.zh: 明日，汴、魏乘勝合兵擊仁恭，破其八寨，仁恭父子燒營而遁。

translations.literal: The next day, Bian and Wei, riding victory, united armies to strike Rengong, broke his eight stockades; Rengong father and son burned camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Bian and Wei troops combined and, pressing their advantage, shattered Liu Rengong's eight camps; Liu Rengong and his son burned their encampment and fled.

sentences.zh: 汴、魏之人長驅追之，至臨清，擁其眾入永濟渠，殺溺不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Bian and Wei men pursued at full drive to Linqing, crowded their masses into the Yongji Canal; slain and drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Wei troops pursued hotly to Linqing and drove the Yan army into the Yongji Canal; the dead and drowned were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 鎮人亦出兵邀擊於東境，自魏至滄五百里間，殭屍相枕。

translations.literal: Zhen men also sent troops to intercept on the eastern border; from Wei to Cang for five hundred li, corpses lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen troops also struck from the east; for five hundred li from Wei to Cangzhou corpses lay stacked along the road.

sentences.zh: 仁恭自是不振，而全忠益橫矣。

translations.literal: From this Rengong did not recover, while Quanzhong grew all the more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong never regained his strength, while Zhu Quanzhong grew more domineering than ever.

sentences.zh: 德倫，河西胡人也，劉仁恭之攻魏州也，羅紹威遣使修好於河東，且求救。

translations.literal: Delun was a Hu man of Hexi; when Liu Rengong attacked Weizhou, Luo Shaowei sent envoys to make peace with Hedong and also to beg for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He Delun was a non-Han from Hexi. When Liu Rengong attacked Weizhou, Luo Shaowei sent envoys to renew ties with Hedong and plead for aid.

sentences.zh: 壬午，李克用遣李嗣昭將兵救之。

translations.literal: On renwu, Li Keyong sent Li Sizhao to lead troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Li Keyong sent Li Sizhao with an army to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 會仁恭已為汴兵所敗，紹威復與河東絕，嗣昭引還。

translations.literal: It happened that Rengong had already been defeated by Bian troops; Shaowei again broke with Hedong; Sizhao led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: By then Liu Rengong had already been beaten by Liang forces; Luo Shaowei broke with Hedong again; Li Sizhao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 葛從周乘破幽州之勢，自土門攻河東，拔承天軍。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou, riding the momentum of defeating Youzhou, from Tumen attacked Hedong and took Chengtian Army post.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou, riding the victory over Yan, attacked Hedong through Tumen and seized Chengtian Fort.

sentences.zh: 別將氏叔琮自馬嶺入，拔遼州樂平，進軍榆次。

translations.literal: Separate commander Shi Shuzong entered from Maling, took Liaozhou's Leping, and advanced the army to Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: His lieutenant Shi Shuzong entered through Maling, took Leping in Liaozhou, and advanced on Yuci.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣內牙軍副周德威擊之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent the vice-commander of the Inner Guard Army, Zhou Dewei, to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent Zhou Dewei, deputy commander of the Inner Guards, to attack them.

sentences.zh: 叔琮有驍將陳章，號「陳夜叉」，為前鋒，請於叔琮曰：「河東所恃者周楊五，請擒之，求一州為賞。」

translations.literal: Shuzong had a fierce general Chen Zhang, called "Chen the Yaksha," as vanguard; he asked Shuzong, "What Hedong relies on is Zhou Yang the Fifth; please let me seize him; I ask one prefecture as reward."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shuzong had a fierce lieutenant Chen Zhang, nicknamed "Chen the Yaksha," in the vanguard; he asked Shi Shuzong, "Hedong's pillar is Zhou Yang the Fifth—let me capture him; grant me a prefecture as reward."

sentences.zh: 克用聞之，以戒德威，德威曰：「彼大言耳。」

translations.literal: Keyong heard it and used it to warn Dewei; Dewei said, "That is big talk."
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong warned Zhou Dewei; Zhou Dewei replied, "He is talking big."

sentences.zh: 戰于洞渦，德威微服往挑戰，謂其屬曰：「汝見陳夜叉即走。」

translations.literal: They fought at Dongwo; Dewei in plain dress went to offer challenge and said to his followers, "When you see Chen the Yaksha, run."
translations.idiomatic: At Dongwo he fought them; Zhou Dewei dressed plainly and rode out to provoke them, telling his men, "When you see Chen the Yaksha, run."

sentences.zh: 章果逐之，德威奮鐵檛擊之墜馬，生擒以獻。

translations.literal: Zhang indeed pursued him; Dewei swung an iron mace, struck him off his horse, and presented him captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang did chase him; Zhou Dewei swung his iron mace, knocked him from his horse, and presented him as a captive.

sentences.zh: 因繫叔琮，大破之，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bound Shuzong and inflicted a great defeat; three thousand heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: He then pinned Shi Shuzong in place and routed the army, taking three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 叔琮棄營走，德威追之，出石會關，又斬千餘級。

translations.literal: Shuzong abandoned camp and fled; Dewei pursued him, passed Shihui Pass, and again cut more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shuzong abandoned his camp and fled; Zhou Dewei pursued him beyond Shihui Pass and took another thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 後周亦引還。

translations.literal: Later Zhou also led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，朱全忠遣河陽節度使丁會攻澤州，下之。

translations.literal: On disi, Zhu Quanzhong sent Heyang military governor Ding Hui to attack Zezhou; he took it.
translations.idiomatic: On disi, Zhu Quanzhong sent Heyang military governor Ding Hui to attack Zezhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 婺州刺史王檀為兩浙所圍，求救於宣歙觀察使田頵。

translations.literal: Wang Tan, prefect of Wuzhou, was besieged by the two Zhes and begged rescue from Xuanshe observation commissioner Tian Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou prefect Wang Tan, besieged by the two Zhes, appealed for help to Xuanshe observation commissioner Tian Yun.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，頵遣行營都指揮使康儒救之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Yun sent campaigning chief commander Kang Ru to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Tian Yun sent his campaigning commander Kang Ru to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲午，置武信軍於遂州，以遂、合等五州隸之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiawu, the Wuxin army was established at Suizhou; Suizhou, Hezhou, and four other prefectures were placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiawu, the court established the Wuxin army at Suizhou, subordinating Suizhou, Hezhou, and three other prefectures to it.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣蕃、漢馬步都指揮使李君慶將兵攻李罕之，己亥，圍潞州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent Li Junqing, commander of the Tangut and Han horse and foot forces, to lead troops against Li Hanzhi. On jihai, he besieged Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent Li Junqing, commander of the Tangut and Han horse and foot forces, to lead troops against Li Hanzhi. On jihai, he besieged Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠出屯河陽，辛丑，遣其將張存敬救之，壬寅，又遣丁會將兵繼之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong went out and encamped at Heyang. On xinchou he sent his general Zhang Cunjing to the rescue; on renyin he sent Ding Hui with troops to follow up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong went out and encamped at Heyang. On xinchou he sent his general Zhang Cunjing to the rescue; on renyin he sent Ding Hui with troops to follow up.

sentences.zh: 大破河東兵，君慶解圍去。

translations.literal: Hedong troops were greatly defeated; Junqing lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong troops were greatly defeated; Li Junqing lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 克用誅君慶及其裨將伊審、李弘襲，以李嗣昭為蕃、漢馬步都指揮使，代之攻潞州。

translations.literal: Keyong executed Junqing and his subordinate generals Yi Shen and Li Hongxi, appointed Li Sizhao commander of the Tangut and Han horse and foot forces in his place, and sent him to attack Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong executed Li Junqing and his subordinate generals Yi Shen and Li Hongxi, appointed Li Sizhao commander of the Tangut and Han horse and foot forces in his place, and sent him to attack Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，康儒等敗兩浙兵於龍丘，擒其將王球，遂取婺州。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Kang Ru and others defeated Liang-Zhe troops at Longqiu, captured their general Wang Qiu, and thereupon took Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Kang Ru and others defeated Liang-Zhe troops at Longqiu, captured their general Wang Qiu, and thereupon took Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，李罕之疾亟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yichou, Li Hanzhi's illness grew critical.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yichou, Li Hanzhi's illness grew critical.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，全忠表罕之為河陽節度使，以丁會為昭義節度使。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Quanzhong memorialized that Hanzhi be made Heyang military governor and Ding Hui be made Zhaoyi military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Zhu Quanzhong memorialized that Li Hanzhi be made Heyang military governor and Ding Hui be made Zhaoyi military governor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又以其將張歸霸守邢州，遣葛從周代會守潞州。

translations.literal: Before long he also had his general Zhang Guiba hold Xingzhou and sent Ge Congzhou to replace Hui in holding Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also had his general Zhang Guiba hold Xingzhou and sent Ge Congzhou to replace Ding Hui in holding Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 以西川大將王宗佶為武信節度使。

translations.literal: Xichuan great general Wang Zongji was made Wuxin military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan senior general Wang Zongji was appointed military governor of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 宗佶，本姓甘，洪州人也。

translations.literal: Zongji was originally surnamed Gan and was a native of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongji was originally surnamed Gan and was a native of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，李罕之薨於懷州。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Li Hanzhi died at Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Li Hanzhi died at Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 保義節度使王珙，性猜忍，雖妻子親近，常不自保。

translations.literal: Baoyi military governor Wang Gong was suspicious and cruel by nature; even toward wife, children, and close kin he could not assure his own safety.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyi military governor Wang Gong was suspicious and cruel by nature; even toward wife, children, and close kin he could not assure his own safety.

sentences.zh: 至是軍亂，為麾下所殺，推都將李璠為留後。

translations.literal: At this time the army mutinied; he was killed by his subordinates, who pushed Commander Li Fan as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the army mutinied; he was killed by his subordinates, who pushed Commander Li Fan as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，朱全忠海州戍將陳海賓請降於楊行密。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhu Quanzhong's Haizhou garrison general Chen Haibin asked to surrender to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhu Quanzhong's Haizhou garrison general Chen Haibin asked to surrender to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 淮海游奕使張訓以漢賓心未可知，與漣水防遏使廬江王綰將兵二千直趣海州，遂據其城。

translations.literal: Huaihai patrol commissioner Zhang Xun, because Haibin's intentions could not be known, joined with Lianshui defense commissioner Wang Wan of Lujiang to lead two thousand troops straight to Haizhou and thereupon seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huaihai patrol commissioner Zhang Xun, because Chen Haibin's intentions could not be known, joined with Lianshui defense commissioner Wang Wan of Lujiang to lead two thousand troops straight to Haizhou and thereupon seized the city.

sentences.zh: 加荊南節度使成汭兼中書令。

translations.literal: Jingnan military governor Cheng Ru was given the additional title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan military governor Cheng Ru was given the additional title of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 馬殷遣其將李唐攻道州，蔡結聚群蠻，伏兵於隘以擊之，大破唐兵。

translations.literal: Ma Yin sent his general Li Tang to attack Daozhou. Cai Jie gathered the tribal peoples, ambushed troops in a pass to strike him, and greatly defeated Tang's army.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin sent his general Li Tang to attack Daozhou. Cai Jie gathered the tribal peoples, ambushed troops in a pass to strike him, and greatly defeated Li Tang's army.

sentences.zh: 唐曰：「蠻所恃者，山林耳。

translations.literal: Tang said: "What the tribes rely on is only the mountain forests.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang said, "What the tribes rely on is only the mountain forests.

sentences.zh: 若戰平地，安能敗我！」

translations.literal: If we fight on level ground, how can they defeat me!"
translations.idiomatic: If we fight on level ground, how can they defeat me!"

sentences.zh: 乃命因風燔林，火燭天地，群蠻驚遁，遂拔道州，擒結，斬之。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered that the forests be burned with the wind; fire lit heaven and earth; the tribes fled in alarm; Daozhou was stormed; Jie was seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered that the forests be burned with the wind; fire lit heaven and earth; the tribes fled in alarm; Daozhou was stormed; Cai Jie was seized and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠召葛從周於潞州，使賀德倫守之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong recalled Ge Congzhou from Luzhou and had He Delun hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong recalled Ge Congzhou from Luzhou and had He Delun hold it.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙寅，李嗣昭引兵至潞州城下，分兵攻澤州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingyin, Li Sizhao led troops to the foot of Luzhou's walls and detached columns to attack Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingyin, Li Sizhao led troops to the foot of Luzhou's walls and detached columns to attack Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 己巳，汴將劉玘棄澤州走，河東兵進拔天井關。

translations.literal: On jisi, Bian general Liu Qi abandoned Zezhou and fled; Hedong troops advanced and stormed Tianjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Bian general Liu Qi abandoned Zezhou and fled; Hedong troops advanced and stormed Tianjing Pass.

sentences.zh: 以李孝璋為澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Xiaozhang was made Prefect of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaozhang was appointed Prefect of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 賀德倫閉城不出，李嗣昭日以鐵騎環其城，捕芻牧者，附城三十里禾黍皆刈之。

translations.literal: He Delun shut the city and would not come out. Li Sizhao daily sent iron cavalry to circle the city, seized those gathering fodder and grazing livestock, and reaped all grain and millet within thirty li of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He Delun shut the city and would not come out. Li Sizhao daily sent iron cavalry to circle the city, seized those gathering fodder and grazing livestock, and reaped all grain and millet within thirty li of the walls.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，德倫等棄城宵遁，趣壺關，河東將李存審伏兵邀擊之，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Delun and the others abandoned the city and fled by night toward Huguan Pass; Hedong general Li Cunshen ambushed them and killed and captured a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, He Delun and the others abandoned the city and fled by night toward Huguan Pass; Hedong general Li Cunshen ambushed them and killed and captured a great multitude.

sentences.zh: 葛從周以援兵至，聞德倫等已敗，乃還。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou came with relief troops; hearing that Delun and the others had already been defeated, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou came with relief troops; hearing that He Delun and the others had already been defeated, he returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸卯，以鳳翔節度使李茂貞為鳳翔、彰義節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guimao, Fengxiang military governor Li Maozhen was made military governor of both Fengxiang and Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guimao, Fengxiang military governor Li Maozhen was made military governor of both Fengxiang and Zhangyi.

sentences.zh: 李克用表汾州刺史孟遷為昭義留後。

translations.literal: Li Keyong memorialized that Fenzhou Prefect Meng Qian be made acting military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong memorialized that Fenzhou Prefect Meng Qian be appointed acting military governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 淄青節度使王師範以沂、密內叛，乞師於楊行密。

translations.literal: Ziqing military governor Wang Shifan, because Yi and Mi rebelled within his circuit, begged troops from Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqing military governor Wang Shifan, because Yi and Mi rebelled within his circuit, begged troops from Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，行密遣海州刺史臺濛、副使王綰將兵助之，拔密州，歸於師範。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Xingmi sent Haizhou Prefect Tai Meng and deputy commissioner Wang Wan to lead troops to assist him; Mizhou was stormed and returned to Shifan's control.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Yang Xingmi sent Haizhou Prefect Tai Meng and deputy commissioner Wang Wan to lead troops to assist him; Mizhou was stormed and returned to Wang Shifan's control.

sentences.zh: 將攻沂州，先使覘之，曰：「城中皆偃旗息鼓。」

translations.literal: About to attack Yizhou, he first sent scouts, who reported: "In the city all banners are lowered and drums stilled."
translations.idiomatic: About to attack Yizhou, he first sent scouts, who reported, "In the city all banners are lowered and drums stilled."

sentences.zh: 綰曰：「此必有備，而救兵近，不可擊也。」

translations.literal: Wan said: "They must certainly be prepared, and relief troops are near—we must not attack."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wan said, "They must certainly be prepared, and relief troops are near—we must not attack."

sentences.zh: 諸將曰：「密已下矣，沂何能為！」

translations.literal: The generals said: "Mi has already fallen—what can Yi do!"
translations.idiomatic: The generals said, "Mi has already fallen—what can Yi do!"

sentences.zh: 綰不能止，乃伏兵林中以待之。

translations.literal: Wan could not stop them and therefore hid troops in the forest to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wan could not stop them and therefore hid troops in the forest to await them.

sentences.zh: 諸將攻沂州不克，救兵至，引退。

translations.literal: The generals attacked Yizhou but could not take it; relief troops arrived and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The generals attacked Yizhou but could not take it; relief troops arrived and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 州兵乘之，綰髮伏擊敗之。

translations.literal: Prefectural troops pursued them; Wan's hidden troops sprang up and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural troops pursued them; Wang Wan's hidden troops sprang up and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，陝州都將朱簡殺李璠，自稱留後，附朱全忠，仍請更名友謙，預於子姪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Shaanzhou commander Zhu Jian killed Li Fan, styled himself acting military governor, submitted to Zhu Quanzhong, and further asked to change his name to Youqian and be enrolled among Zhu's sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Shaanzhou commander Zhu Jian killed Li Fan, styled himself acting military governor, submitted to Zhu Quanzhong, and further asked to change his name to Youqian and be enrolled among Zhu's sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 加忠義節度使趙匡凝兼中書令。

translations.literal: Zhongyi military governor Zhao Kuangning was given the additional title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi military governor Zhao Kuangning was given the additional title of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 馬殷遣其將李瓊攻郴州，執陳彥謙，斬之；

translations.literal: Ma Yin sent his general Li Qiong to attack Chenzhou, seized Chen Yanqian, and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin sent his general Li Qiong to attack Chenzhou, seized Chen Yanqian, and beheaded him;

sentences.zh: 進攻連州，魯景仁自殺，湖南皆平。

translations.literal: he advanced to attack Lianzhou; Lu Jingren killed himself; all of Hunan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: he advanced to attack Lianzhou; Lu Jingren killed himself; all of Hunan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十二月，加魏博節度使羅紹威同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Weibo military governor Luo Shaowei was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Weibo military governor Luo Shaowei was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councillor.
